summary: Players manage a network of workers moving along a branching space-gate structure to claim actions, then race to build efficient settlements on modular exoplanet boards. It plays as a tight worker-placement/tile-laying engine-builder where positioning on the gate track matters as much as the actions themselves.
praised: The space-gate movement mechanism is inventive and central to strategy, not just a theme skin
Strong, well-integrated theme with modular double-sided planet boards for replayability
Satisfying puzzle of route-building and timing when your worker "jumps" to a planet
Good production quality and component design
criticised: Rules overhead and setup are fiddly for the depth of play
Can feel a bit dry/mechanical with limited narrative tension between turns
Some objective/scoring cards are stronger than others, creating imbalance
Downtime and AP-prone decision points in higher player counts

interaction.kind: indirect blocking via shared gate positions and planet spot competition

scoring.why: Points come from multiple sources: settlement placement bonuses, completed objectives, resource/technology tracks, and end-game scoring cards, so the winner is usually whoever balances several engines rather than maxing one.
